system: Tailwind CSS v4, semantic CSS-variable tokens mapped via @theme, toggled by a .dark class (not prefers-color-scheme).
rules: Never use hardcoded Tailwind palette colors (text-blue-500, bg-red-500, border-gray-200, etc.) or inline hex/rgb colors in generated UI.
Always use the semantic token classes below (bg-primary, text-foreground, border-border, ...) so generated UI automatically follows the consumer's theme in both light and dark mode.

Every base token except background/foreground/border/input/ring has a matching '-foreground' token for text/icons placed on top of it (e.g. bg-primary + text-primary-foreground, bg-destructive + text-destructive-foreground).

Page background: bg-background. Card surfaces: bg-card. A distinct section within a page (not the whole page, not a card): bg-accent, or bg-card again if it needs to read as a panel. Popovers/dropdowns/tooltips: bg-popover. Never use bg-muted as a page, section, or card background — muted is reserved for non-surface fills only (skeleton placeholders, disabled-state fills, inline code backgrounds), not for anything a user reads content on top of.
Status colors: success (positive/confirmation), warning (caution), info (neutral notice), destructive (danger/errors) — use these instead of ad-hoc green/yellow/blue/red.

Dark mode requires no extra work in generated code: the same class names resolve to the .dark palette automatically because the consumer's CSS defines both blocks. Do not write dark: variants for color — only use dark: for things the token system doesn't cover (rare).
antiAiLookRules: This section exists because AI-generated UI has recognizable tells. Read it before generating anything visual — the goal is UI indistinguishable from a deliberate human design pass, not a demo that screams 'built by an LLM'.

No gradients on backgrounds, buttons, or text (bg-gradient-to-r, from-purple-500 to-pink-500, bg-clip-text text-transparent, etc.). Use a flat bg-primary (or the relevant status token) instead. This is the single most common AI-UI tell — do not use it even 'just for one hero section'.

No shadows. Don't add box-shadow/drop-shadow utilities (shadow-sm through shadow-2xl, glowing hover rings, colored blur halos) to buttons, badges, cards, inputs, or any static surface — a flat surface with border-border is correct. If a floating layer (modal, popover, dropdown menu) needs visual separation from what's behind it, a border plus the surface's own background token (bg-popover, bg-card) is enough; don't reach for shadow as the default way to show elevation.

No blur effects. Don't use backdrop-blur or any glassmorphism treatment (frosted-glass cards, translucent bg-white/10 panels) anywhere in generated UI, including modal backdrops — use an opaque or semi-opaque solid backdrop (e.g. bg-background/80) instead of a blurred one. Surfaces are opaque (bg-card, bg-popover, bg-background), not translucent.

No blanket border-radius escalation — don't reach for rounded-2xl/rounded-3xl/rounded-full on every card, input, and button by default. Match the radius already used by the surrounding neuctra-ui components (rounded-md/rounded-lg/rounded-xl per component, see each component's own classes) instead of picking a bigger one because it 'looks more modern'.

No decorative hover/focus glow rings. ring-* and focus-visible:ring-ring exist for accessibility (keyboard focus indication) only — never add a colored ring or glow as a pointer-hover decoration on cards, buttons, or images.

No animate-pulse / bounce / scale-105-on-hover / floating-icon motion sprinkled across static content as decoration. Motion should communicate state (loading, a toast entering, a modal opening) — components already handle that internally. Don't add extra hover-scale or idle animation to elements that aren't interactive or aren't mid-transition.

No emoji used as icons or bullet markers in generated UI (✨, 🚀, 💡, ✅ as list bullets, feature markers, or button icons). Use lucide-react icons — the same icon set every neuctra-ui component already uses — passed via each component's icon props (iconBefore, iconAfter, icon, etc.).

No 'icon in a colored circle badge' repeated on every single feature/stat/card by default (a bg-primary/10 rounded-full p-3 wrapper around every icon). Use it sparingly, only where the component's own design already calls for it — repeating the same decorative wrapper on every card in a grid is a generic-template tell.
No arbitrary one-off spacing/sizing values (p-[13px], gap-[7px], w-[327px]) — use the Tailwind spacing scale (p-3, gap-2, w-80, etc.) so spacing stays consistent with the rest of the design system.

Prefer information density and restraint over generic centered-hero-with-huge-padding layouts. Not every section needs max-w-7xl mx-auto text-center py-24 — match the density and layout the consumer's existing UI already uses.

Make every layout fully responsive by default — mobile, tablet, and desktop (sm:/md:/lg:/xl: breakpoints), stacking to a single column and adjusting spacing/type-scale at small widths. Never ship a fixed-width or desktop-only layout and call it done.

No em dashes (—) in generated copy or UI text (headings, body copy, button labels, placeholder text). It's a recognizable AI-writing tell. Use a period, comma, colon, or restructure the sentence instead.

No over-effects: don't stack multiple decorative treatments on one element (e.g. a gradient plus a shadow plus a hover-scale plus a glow, all on the same button). Every visual effect that does appear should communicate a real state or interaction (hover, focus, loading, an entering toast) — never decoration for its own sake.

Use correct line-height and letter-spacing for readability. Body text: leading-relaxed or leading-normal, never leading-none/leading-tight on paragraphs. Letter-spacing: leave at the default (tracking-normal) for body and headings; only use tracking-wide for short uppercase labels (badges, eyebrow text, nav labels), and never tracking-wide on paragraph-length text.

The bar is modern, visually appealing UI — achieved through typography hierarchy, whitespace, correct token usage, and responsive layout, not through gradients, shadows, blur, or glow effects standing in for actual design decisions.

When unsure whether an effect (shadow, gradient, blur, glow, animation) is warranted: leave it out. A flat, token-colored, appropriately-radiused, unshadowed, responsive surface is the correct default for the overwhelming majority of neuctra-ui components.

tokens.usage: Brand color: primary buttons, active states, links, focus accents.
Subtle/secondary surfaces (skeletons, disabled fills, code blocks).
Hover/active background for interactive rows and menu items.
Default border color for inputs, cards, dividers.
Focus ring color — always pair interactive elements with focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring.
Card / panel surfaces, distinct from the page background.
Errors, delete/danger actions, invalid form states.
Confirmation, online status, valid form states, positive metrics.
Caution states, pending status, non-blocking alerts.

note: Values shown are the CLI-generated defaults (npx @neuctra/ui-cli init). A consumer project may have redefined these hex values in its own CSS — the token NAMES and pairing rules are the stable contract; always prefer the class names over the hex values.

whatItDoes: Checks React (upgrades to >=18 if needed) and Tailwind CSS (upgrades to v4 if needed) — @neuctra/ui requires Tailwind v4 syntax (@theme, @source, @custom-variant).
Writes/updates the project's global CSS with the token blocks shown in this response (:root + .dark + @theme mapping) and the correct @source path for the project's own layout.

Generates a theme context file at src/contexts/ThemeContext.jsx (or .tsx if the project is TypeScript) exporting ThemeProvider and useTheme — handles localStorage persistence, system-preference detection with live updates, and avoids a flash of the wrong theme on load.
Wraps the app's entry point in <ThemeProvider>.
setup.whenToSuggestIt: If a project doesn't have @neuctra/ui installed yet, or has no theme token CSS / no ThemeContext, suggest running this command instead of hand-writing the CSS token blocks or a theme context from scratch — it is the maintained, correct source for both.
setup.manualSetupStillDocumented: If the consumer can't run a CLI (e.g. you're only shown existing code, not given shell access), the full manual step-by-step — including the exact ThemeContext implementation the CLI generates — is at the project's /docs/full-setup page (FullSetupDocPage) and is safe to reproduce by hand.

toastNote: @neuctra/ui's toast notification system is a standalone function, not hook-only: import { toast, ToastProvider } from '@neuctra/ui' and call toast(...) / toast.success(...) / toast.error(...) / toast.warning(...) / toast.info(...) / toast.loading(...) / toast.promise(...) from anywhere — event handlers, API clients, utility files — no useToast() hook required at the call site. Mount <ToastProvider> once near the app root so there is somewhere for toasts to render; mounting it more than once duplicates every toast. useToast() still exists for consumers who prefer a hook — it returns the identical global toast/dismiss, so both styles stay in sync. See get_component with name "ToastProvider" for the full prop list (including position, one of top-left/top-center/top-right/bottom-left/bottom-center/bottom-right).
